name: Coast Commons
author: Claude, at Mike Hoydich's request
what: An open study of community-run shared houses, clubhouses and boats for the beach towns within about 25 miles of El Segundo, California, with each town's official rules pages.
notice: A study and a public resource, not an offer.
Nothing is being bought or sold. No money is being raised. No listings.
Not legal, tax or investment advice.
Tradable shares in property are likely securities and need a securities lawyer.

licence.proposal: CC BY 4.0 for the words, drawings and this file
licence.decision: Left for Mike Hoydich. No LICENSE file has been added.

method.distance: Straight-line (great-circle, haversine) miles from the origin to one approximate reference point per town. Not driving distance.
method.rules: Each rule summary is a short paraphrase of a page opened on the verified date. Entries with verified:false were not checked and carry no source.

hosted.label: Hosted rooms only
hosted.note: A resident host must be home. No whole-house weekends.

none.label: No short stays in homes
none.note: Short stays are barred in residential zones.

narrow.label: A few permitted homes
narrow.note: Only permitted homes in certain commercial zones.

split.label: Depends on the Coastal Zone
split.note: Banned outside it; a court held the ban does not reach inside it.

registered.label: Registered homes
registered.note: Lawful only in a home the host has registered with the city.

permit.label: Permitted homes
permit.note: Lawful only in a home holding a city permit.

capped.label: Capped permits
capped.note: A small fixed number of permitted homes.

pending.label: Rules pending
pending.note: County rules were waiting on the Coastal Commission.

towns.name: Malibu

character.summary: Surfrider Beach has almost a mile of ocean frontage and became famous through the surf films of the 1950s and 60s. Next to it, Malibu Lagoon is 22 acres of wetland used by more than 200 bird species.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: Malibu Surfrider Beach

character.summary: Topanga Beach, at the east end, breaks over cobblestone and reef and suits surfing more than swimming.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: Topanga Beach

towns.commons_sketch: A board barn more than a bunkhouse: a shared rack of longboards and wetsuits near the point, a rinse station, a bench, and a logbook. Members drive in for the morning and go home. The public-good share could be a monthly lagoon bird walk and beach clean.

short_term_rentals.summary: Since January 15, 2021 a City short-term rental permit is required to advertise or operate one (Ordinance 468, Municipal Code Chapter 17.55). A stricter hosted ordinance (472), with an on-site host and primary residence rule, was adopted in 2020 but waits on Coastal Commission certification; the page calls it in progress.

sources.label: City of Malibu: short-term rental program

adus.summary: ADU rules are in Municipal Code 17.44 and the coastal implementation plan. The page says all of Malibu is in the Coastal Zone and its certified Local Coastal Program governs new development, ADUs included. A coastal amendment for ADUs was sent to the Coastal Commission in February 2024; its status was not stated.

sources.label: City of Malibu: accessory dwelling units

coastal_permits.summary: All of Malibu is in the Coastal Zone and the City has a certified Local Coastal Program, per the City's ADU page. The City's coastal permit page was not opened.

sources.label: City of Malibu: accessory dwelling units

zoning.summary: Not verified. The zoning map and code were not opened.

towns.name: Santa Monica

character.summary: Not verified. No official beach page was opened for Santa Monica State Beach. Generally known: a wide, flat city beach with a pier, a bike path and gentle beach-break waves that suit beginners.

towns.commons_sketch: A hosted house. One member household that already lives here holds the home-share permit and hosts a room or two; the commons is the garage: boards, bikes, a repair stand. The public-good share could be free loaner boards for a beginners' morning.

short_term_rentals.summary: Home-sharing means renting bedrooms for 30 days or less in the host's primary residence with the host living on site throughout. It needs a home-share permit and a business license. The City's rules treat a stay with no host on site as a prohibited vacation rental.

sources.label: City of Santa Monica: how to apply for a home-share business license
City of Santa Monica: Home-Sharing Ordinance rules and regulations (PDF, revised Nov 21, 2019)

adus.summary: The planning resources page carries ADU guides dated November 2025 for single-unit and multi-unit parcels, and a pre-approved ADU program.

sources.label: City of Santa Monica: planning resources

coastal_permits.summary: The planning resources page links the Local Coastal Program land use plans of 1992 and 2018 and an update page. Who issues coastal development permits in Santa Monica was not verified.

sources.label: City of Santa Monica: planning resources

zoning.summary: The same page links an interactive zoning district lookup and the zoning ordinance.

sources.label: City of Santa Monica: planning resources

towns.name: Venice

character.summary: About three miles of coast and 238 acres of sand along Ocean Front Walk. The County calls the Venice Breakwater a well-regarded local surf spot.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: Venice Beach

towns.commons_sketch: A workshop with a couch. A ding-repair and shaping bay, a music corner, a wall of shared boards. Sleeping is secondary; making things is the point. The public-good share could be a free monthly repair clinic.

short_term_rentals.summary: Under the Home-Sharing Ordinance a host may share only their primary residence, must register with the City and show the number on listings, and is limited to 120 days a year unless they hold an extended registration. Rent-stabilized units are not eligible, and renters need the landlord's notarized approval.

sources.label: Los Angeles City Planning: Home-Sharing Program

adus.summary: Not verified. The City's ADU pages were not opened.

coastal_permits.summary: The Venice Local Coastal Program is not certified: its land use plan was certified in 2001, the implementation plan was not. The Venice Coastal Zone Specific Plan (1999, revised 2004) sets use and density. Who signs coastal permits today was not stated on the page.

sources.label: Los Angeles City Planning: Venice Local Coastal Program

zoning.summary: Not verified. The City's zoning map tools were not opened.

towns.name: Marina del Rey

character.summary: Mother's Beach is a human-made beach inside the harbor with nearly half a mile of sand and no surf in the swimming area. Kayaking and windsurfing are the main activities.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: Marina (Mother's) Beach

towns.commons_sketch: A boat, not a house. A shared small sailboat or a rack of kayaks and paddleboards with a booking sheet. The same recipe applies: ten people, open books, use-rights. The public-good share could be free harbor paddles for kids who have never been on the water.

short_term_rentals.summary: The County's short-term rental ordinance took effect October 7, 2024 for unincorporated areas, with registration of a primary residence only. The County page says it does not apply in coastal areas, Marina del Rey included, until the Coastal Commission approves it and it is written into each Local Coastal Program. Whether that has happened since was not verified.

sources.label: Los Angeles County Treasurer and Tax Collector: short-term rentals

adus.summary: The same County page says ADUs and junior ADUs cannot be used as short-term rentals under the ordinance, and that the County's Title 22 ADU rules do not apply in the coastal zone. Marina del Rey's own coastal rules were not opened.

sources.label: Los Angeles County Treasurer and Tax Collector: short-term rentals

coastal_permits.summary: Marina del Rey has a certified Local Coastal Program (1984, amended 2012), so coastal permits are handled by the County, with the Coastal Commission keeping tidelands and certain appeals. This comes from a County archive page that points to the current planning site for updates.

sources.label: Los Angeles County Regional Planning: coastal (archive page)

zoning.summary: Not verified. The current Marina del Rey land use plan and zoning pages were not opened.

towns.name: Playa del Rey

character.summary: Dockweiler has 3.7 miles of ocean frontage and 288 acres of beach, fire rings, a hang gliding area, and an RV campground with more than 100 full hook-up spaces. The Marvin Braude Bike Trail runs alongside.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: Dockweiler Beach

towns.commons_sketch: A house on wheels. The County campground is a lawful place for a group to spend a weekend by the water, so the first step here could be a few campsites and a fire ring rather than a rental house. The public-good share could be a fire-ring supper open to anyone who brings a dish.

short_term_rentals.summary: Under the Home-Sharing Ordinance a host may share only their primary residence, must register with the City and show the number on listings, and is limited to 120 days a year unless they hold an extended registration. Rent-stabilized units are not eligible, and renters need the landlord's notarized approval.

sources.label: Los Angeles City Planning: Home-Sharing Program

adus.summary: Not verified. The City's ADU pages were not opened.

coastal_permits.summary: Not verified. The coastal permit path for this part of the City of Los Angeles was not opened.

zoning.summary: Not verified. The City's zoning map tools were not opened.

towns.name: El Segundo

character.summary: Not verified. No official page for El Segundo Beach was opened. Generally known: a short city shoreline along Vista del Mar between Dockweiler and Manhattan Beach, beside the refinery and the power plant, reached from the foot of Grand Avenue and by the bike path. The town itself sits on the bluff above.

towns.commons_sketch: The flagship study. See the full page.

short_term_rentals.summary: The City runs a home share permit. A homeowner may rent bedrooms for 30 days or less in the home they live in, and must be living there during the stay. The page caps guests at six on the parcel, bars parties and events, bars short stays in an ADU, and lists a permit registration fee of $396 and a renewal fee of $201. A whole house rented to a group for a weekend with no owner present is not what this permit covers.

sources.label: City of El Segundo: home share rental permit

adus.summary: The City says ADUs are allowed by right in any zone that allows housing, with standards in Municipal Code sections 15-4E-3 (ADUs) and 15-4F-2 (JADUs). It offers an application handout, a fee calculator and pre-approved plans.

sources.label: City of El Segundo: ADU and JADU resources

coastal_permits.summary: The planning applications page lists a Coastal Development application guide. A third-party copy of Municipal Code Title 15, Chapter 26 says a coastal development permit is needed before development in the Coastal Zone and that the Planning Commission grants it. The adopted code itself was not opened.

sources.label: City of El Segundo: planning applications
El Segundo Municipal Code, Title 15 Chapter 26 (third-party copy, October 2026 edition)

zoning.summary: Not verified. The zoning map and the adopted zoning code were not opened. The planning applications page says to email Planning staff.

towns.name: Manhattan Beach

character.summary: More than two miles of ocean frontage, a 900-foot pier, and volleyball nets running south to Hermosa. The north end, El Porto, is a popular surf spot where lessons are offered.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: Manhattan Beach

towns.commons_sketch: A dawn-patrol locker room near El Porto: racks, hot rinse, coffee, out by eight. A weekend house is only a live question inside the Coastal Zone, and that needs a lawyer's reading first. The public-good share could be free youth surf mornings with borrowed boards.

short_term_rentals.summary: The City defines a short-term rental as under 30 days and bans it in residential zones (Ordinance 19-0007, 2019). The page says a Court of Appeal opinion of April 4, 2022 held the ban does not apply inside the Coastal Zone, where operators need a business license and must remit hotel tax. When the page was read it also described a temporary World Cup allowance outside the Coastal Zone as under Council consideration in January 2026; the outcome was not verified.

sources.label: City of Manhattan Beach: short-term rentals

adus.summary: Ordinance 25-0004 took effect May 1, 2025. ADUs are allowed in single-family and multi-family zones and JADUs in single-family zones, inside or outside the Coastal Zone. Until the Coastal Commission certifies the matching coastal amendments, the page says units in the Coastal Zone follow state law only.

sources.label: City of Manhattan Beach: ADUs and JADUs

coastal_permits.summary: The City publishes its Local Coastal Program, including Chapter A.96 on coastal development permit procedures and application instructions. Recent amendments are listed as awaiting Coastal Commission certification.

sources.label: City of Manhattan Beach: Local Coastal Program

zoning.summary: The zoning code is Title 10 of the Municipal Code. The City posts a zoning map that shows the coastal zone, and an interactive parcel map.

sources.label: City of Manhattan Beach: zoning and development regulations

towns.name: Hermosa Beach

character.summary: Almost two miles of city-owned beach, known for surf and swimming, with The Strand along the sand and a concrete pier first built in 1913.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: Hermosa Beach

towns.commons_sketch: A music room over a board room. Hermosa is where a clubhouse in a commercial district makes more sense than a house on a walk street: instruments upstairs, boards and volleyballs downstairs. The public-good share could be an open jam and a free ball-and-net loan.

short_term_rentals.summary: Stays under 30 days are allowed only in older, lawfully established homes that sit in commercial zones C-2 and C-3 and specific plan areas 7, 8 and 11, and only with an administrative permit. Operating without one carries fines that start at $5,000.

sources.label: City of Hermosa Beach: short-term vacation rentals

adus.summary: ADU rules are in Municipal Code Chapter 17.21. Rentals must run at least 30 days, so an ADU cannot be a short-term rental.

sources.label: City of Hermosa Beach: accessory dwelling units

coastal_permits.summary: Hermosa Beach has a certified coastal land use plan but not a fully certified Local Coastal Program. The City approves a project in concept and the Coastal Commission's South Coast District issues the coastal development permit.

sources.label: City of Hermosa Beach: Local Coastal Plan

zoning.summary: Not verified. The zoning map and code pages were not opened.

towns.name: Redondo Beach

character.summary: A mile and a half of beach south of the horseshoe pier, good for surfing, swimming and windsurfing, with King Harbor to the north. A statue of surfing pioneer George Freeth stands at the pier.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: Redondo Beach

towns.commons_sketch: A community kitchen by the harbor. A rented commercial kitchen day, a long table, and a paddle rack. The public-good share could be a monthly free supper cooked by members.

short_term_rentals.summary: A City document treats lodging for 30 days or less as a hotel or motel use, which the municipal code bars in the single-family and multi-family residential zones (sections 10-2.402, 10-2.501 and 10-2.511). The document carries no date.

sources.label: City of Redondo Beach: short-term rentals not permitted in residential zones (PDF)

adus.summary: Not verified. The planning forms page links to an ADU page, which was not opened.

coastal_permits.summary: Not verified. The City's coastal permit pages were not opened.

zoning.summary: The planning page links the zoning ordinance, a GIS map and a 2025 zoning map PDF.

sources.label: City of Redondo Beach: planning procedures and forms

towns.name: Torrance Beach

character.summary: About 40 acres of soft sand under the cliffs that run to the Palos Verdes Peninsula. The stretch shared with Redondo is often called RAT Beach.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: Torrance Beach

towns.commons_sketch: A hosted house with a garden. Torrance allows a home share when the host lives on site, so the pattern here is a member family that hosts, plus a shared vegetable plot and a tool shed. The public-good share could be a seed and tool library.

short_term_rentals.summary: In residential zones the only short-term rental allowed is a home share with the host living on site for the whole stay. Commercial zones allow them with or without a host. A City permit and business license are required. In the Coastal Zone the rules follow the Coastal Commission approval the page cites as CDP 5-20-0031.

sources.label: City of Torrance: short term rentals

adus.summary: ADU rules are in Municipal Code section 92.2.10, amended in October 2025. An ADU may not be rented for less than 30 days. For the Coastal Zone the page sends applicants to the Coastal Commission.

sources.label: City of Torrance: accessory dwelling units

coastal_permits.summary: The land use page lists a Hillside and Local Coastal Overlay with its own boundaries and review procedure. The overlay page itself was not opened.

sources.label: City of Torrance: land use plans and standards

zoning.summary: Not verified. The land use page does not link a zoning map; none was opened.

towns.name: Palos Verdes Estates

character.summary: Not verified. No official page was opened for the coves. Generally known: rocky reef and point breaks under high bluffs, reached by steep trails.

towns.commons_sketch: No house. A stewardship crew with a shared shed: trail tools, tide-pool guides, a first-aid kit. The commons is the cove itself and the habit of looking after it. The public-good share is the work.

short_term_rentals.summary: The City lists short term or vacation rentals in the R1 zone as a common code violation and cites Municipal Code section 18.04.021. The code section itself was not opened.

sources.label: City of Palos Verdes Estates: common code enforcement violations

adus.summary: Local ADU rules are in Municipal Code Chapter 18.45, adopted by Ordinance O20-747 in October 2020. The process can include a recorded deed restriction and a yearly rent certification.

sources.label: City of Palos Verdes Estates: ADUs

coastal_permits.summary: Not verified. No City coastal permit page was opened.

zoning.summary: Not verified. The zoning map and code were not opened.

towns.name: Rancho Palos Verdes

character.summary: Not verified. No official page was opened for the shoreline. Generally known: coves, tide pools and bluff-top trails rather than sand beaches.

towns.commons_sketch: A garden and a trailhead. Short stays are barred in homes here, so the pattern is a day commons: a shared garden plot, a native plant nursery bench, a walking group. The public-good share could be free tide-pool mornings led by members.

short_term_rentals.summary: The City Council affirmed in 2016 that rentals under 30 days are prohibited in residential zones, and Ordinances 592U and 593 also bar advertising them. Fines listed run from $2,500 to $7,500.

sources.label: City of Rancho Palos Verdes: short term rentals

adus.summary: ADUs are allowed on lots zoned for single-family or multi-family housing and JADUs on single-family lots, under Municipal Code Chapter 17.10. The page noted a Council item on October 6, 2026 to begin updating the ordinance.

sources.label: City of Rancho Palos Verdes: ADUs and JADUs

coastal_permits.summary: The City has its own Coastal Permit application, required for most improvements on property seaward of Palos Verdes Drive West and South.

sources.label: City of Rancho Palos Verdes: planning applications

zoning.summary: The planning applications page carries a development standards handout for each single-family zone. The zoning map was not opened.

sources.label: City of Rancho Palos Verdes: planning applications

towns.name: San Pedro

character.summary: White Point and Royal Palms have more than a mile and a half of rocky shore with some of the most varied tide pools in Southern California. Fishing, surfing and diving are popular; swimming is not advised. Construction limits parking through 2027.

sources.label: LA County Beaches and Harbors: White Point and Royal Palms

towns.commons_sketch: A workshop near the working harbor: wood, fiberglass, sailcloth, and a shared skiff. The public-good share could be a free boat-building Saturday for teenagers.

short_term_rentals.summary: Under the Home-Sharing Ordinance a host may share only their primary residence, must register with the City and show the number on listings, and is limited to 120 days a year unless they hold an extended registration. Rent-stabilized units are not eligible, and renters need the landlord's notarized approval.

sources.label: Los Angeles City Planning: Home-Sharing Program

adus.summary: Not verified. The City's ADU pages were not opened.

coastal_permits.summary: Not verified. The coastal permit path for this part of the City of Los Angeles was not opened.

zoning.summary: Not verified. The City's zoning map tools were not opened.

towns.name: Long Beach

character.summary: Not verified. No official beach page was opened. Generally known: a long, flat city beach sheltered by the harbor breakwater, with little surf and steady wind, used for kiting, paddling, sailing and rowing.

towns.commons_sketch: The most room on this coast for a lawful first weekend, because registered short-term rentals exist here in number. The house could lean to wind and flat water: kites, paddleboards, a rowing shell. The public-good share could be free paddle mornings.

short_term_rentals.summary: Short-term rentals must be registered. A primary residence can host without limit when the registrant is on site, and for up to 90 days a registration period when not. Registrations for homes that are not a primary residence are capped at 800 citywide. ADUs cannot be short-term rentals. The page lists the fee as $400 in one place and $500 in another.

sources.label: City of Long Beach: short-term rentals

adus.summary: Long Beach applies state ADU law directly while its own ordinance is rewritten. In the Coastal Zone an administrative local coastal development permit comes before the building permit.

sources.label: City of Long Beach: ADUs

coastal_permits.summary: The Local Coastal Program was certified in 1980. The City issues coastal permits in most of its coastal zone, some areas stay with the Coastal Commission, and City decisions in the appealable area can be appealed to the Commission.

sources.label: City of Long Beach: coastal planning

zoning.summary: Not verified. The zoning map and code pages were not opened.

towns.name: Seal Beach

character.summary: Not verified. No official beach page was opened. Generally known: a small-town beach with a long wooden pier and beach-break surf beside it, just across the Orange County line.

towns.commons_sketch: A small clubhouse off Main Street rather than a house, since only a few dozen permitted rentals exist. Boards, a table, a pot of coffee. The public-good share could be free pier-side surf mornings for local kids.

short_term_rentals.summary: Stays of 29 nights or fewer need a City permit and business license, are allowed only in the Coastal Zone south of Westminster Boulevard, and are capped at one percent of homes there. The FAQ counts 31 permits, first awarded by lottery in May 2023, with a waitlist. It lists a $600 first-year fee and $400 renewal. Permits do not transfer on sale.

sources.label: City of Seal Beach: short-term rental FAQ (PDF)
City of Seal Beach: short term rental permits

adus.summary: Not verified. The City's ADU pages were not opened.

coastal_permits.summary: Seal Beach has no certified Local Coastal Program; a revised draft land use plan went to the Coastal Commission for comment on May 9, 2023. The page says the City takes over permitting only after certification, so permits appear to remain with the Commission.

sources.label: City of Seal Beach: Local Coastal Plan project

zoning.summary: Not verified. The zoning map and code were not opened.

left_out.name: Pacific Palisades
left_out.why: About 11 miles out and inside the City of Los Angeles. Left off for now while the neighborhood rebuilds after the January 2025 fire.

left_out.name: Sunset Beach and Huntington Beach
left_out.why: Sunset Beach is about 24 miles out and is part of Huntington Beach, whose pier is about 29 miles out. Treated as outside the circle.

left_out.name: Western Malibu (Zuma, Point Dume and beyond)
left_out.why: Zuma is about 24 miles out and the city continues west past 30. Malibu is measured at Surfrider.

left_out.name: Carson, Lomita, Rolling Hills, Rolling Hills Estates
left_out.why: Inside the circle but with no ocean beach of their own.

notice: This is a study and a public resource. It is not an offer.
Nothing is being bought or sold. No money is being raised. No entity has been formed, and no house, land or animal has been chosen.
It is not legal, tax, health or investment advice.
Tradable shares in property are likely securities. Anyone going near that needs a securities lawyer first.
Distributing milk from unlicensed animals is unlawful in California, whether it is sold, shared or given away.
Rules change. Every source here was opened on November 11, 2026; open the linked page and ask the agency or a licensed professional before acting on any of it.
studies.method: Every source was opened on 2026-11-11 and is linked beside the claim it supports. Paraphrase only. No private individuals are named, and a business is named only where the page links its own site or an official page. What could not be verified is listed here and repeated on the page beside the claim it affects.

list.title: SB Surf House
list.summary: What a community-run surf house on the Santa Barbara coast would take: place, market medians and indices, city, county and coastal rules, eight ways to own together, the securities question, what happened to earlier attempts, three schematic plans, a per-member cost calculator and a nine-step ladder that starts with a rented weekend.
not_verified: The City of Santa Barbara's adopted short-term rental ordinances: read through a news report, a tax-service summary and a City notice, not the ordinance text. The two summaries differ on single-family zones.
Santa Barbara County's ordinance page: only its navigation loaded. County rules rest on an April 2025 press release and a 2018 Coastal Commission staff report.
Carpinteria's four licence caps: from a third-party copy of the municipal code. The City's 2025 policy document confirms the structure, not the numbers.
The SEC's March 2026 interpretive release: read through a law-firm summary, not the release.
No rule specific to surf clubs or membership houses was found in the three jurisdictions; an absence of evidence only.
Whether a members' house with rotating use would be classed as a timeshare, a boarding house or a single household.
Insurance, upkeep, utilities, down payment and member count in the calculator are assumptions.
Wave descriptions come from a single surf guide.

list.title: Fresh Milk, Local
list.summary: California dairy law in plain terms, what federal and state health agencies say about raw milk, which South Bay towns allow cows, goats or sheep, what dairy exists near Los Angeles, precedents elsewhere, a ladder of six options from a buying club to a teaching farm, and a calculator for how many animals a group of households would need.
sections: Six things the reading turned up
not_verified: El Segundo: only the cover page of the city code loaded. Animal and zoning sections not read; no rule is stated.
Manhattan Beach: the municipal code viewer did not load; no rule is stated.
Redondo Beach: only the article list of the animal chapter was read, on a third-party copy; no rule is stated.
Los Angeles Municipal Code § 12.07: seen as a search-index excerpt; the page itself was blocked.
California Food and Agricultural Code § 32505: read from a government-document index, not the official page.
The CDFA milk products plant licence page and the Hermosa Beach animal FAQ could not be opened.
Any current CDFA position on herd shares.
The 2026 status of the Montebello bottler, the Ontario goat dairy, the Compton teaching farm and the milk delivery routes; the reports are from 2017 to 2024.
Whether a buying club or a refill station itself needs a state or county licence.
